canon.title: Achievement of Target Gain Larger than Unity in an Inertial Fusion Experiment
canon.why: 2.05 MJ of laser light in, 3.1 MJ of fusion out. Seventy years of trying, finally over the line.

canon.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
canon.why: A fifty-year-old problem, largely solved. The structures are free for every known protein.

canon.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
canon.why: GPT-3. The paper where scaling alone started producing abilities nobody trained for.

canon.title: Attention Is All You Need
canon.why: The transformer. Every large language model in use today is a descendant of this one paper.

canon.title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger
canon.why: Spacetime itself was measured ringing, a century after Einstein said it would.

canon.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
canon.why: Skip connections made very deep networks trainable. Almost everything since is built on them.

canon.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
canon.why: Two networks trained against each other — the idea that made generated images convincing.

canon.title: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson
canon.why: The last missing piece of the Standard Model, found 48 years after it was predicted.

canon.title: A Programmable Dual-RNA–Guided DNA Endonuclease in Adaptive Bacterial Immunity
canon.who: Jinek, Chylinski, Fonfara, Hauer, Doudna and Charpentier
canon.why: CRISPR-Cas9 turned from a bacterial immune system into a tool for editing any genome.

canon.title: Suppression of RNA Recognition by Toll-like Receptors
canon.why: The modified-nucleoside trick that stops the body attacking mRNA. Ignored for years, then it made the COVID vaccines work.

canon.title: Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe
canon.why: The expansion is speeding up, and nobody knows why. Dark energy is the name for not knowing.

canon.title: Evidence for Oscillation of Atmospheric Neutrinos
canon.why: Neutrinos change type as they travel, which means they have mass — the Standard Model said they did not.

canon.title: LixCoO2: A new cathode material for batteries of high energy density
canon.why: The cathode inside the lithium-ion battery in your phone. A Nobel, 39 years later.

canon.title: The hippocampus as a spatial map
canon.why: The discovery of place cells — the brain's internal map. Nobel Prize 2014.

canon.title: Self-Consistent Equations Including Exchange and Correlation Effects
canon.why: The practical form of density functional theory — how most of computational chemistry works today.

canon.title: A Measurement of Excess Antenna Temperature at 4080 Mc/s
canon.why: They thought it was pigeon droppings in the antenna. It was the afterglow of the Big Bang.

canon.title: Receptive fields, binocular interaction and functional architecture in the cat's visual cortex
canon.why: How the visual cortex builds edges and shapes out of spots of light — and an inspiration for convolutional networks.

canon.title: Detailed Balance Limit of Efficiency of p-n Junction Solar Cells
canon.why: Why a single solar cell tops out near a third of the sunlight it catches — and why tandems exist.

canon.title: Experimental Test of Parity Conservation in Beta Decay
canon.why: Nature tells left from right. Physicists had assumed for decades that it could not.

canon.title: Synthesis of the Elements in Stars
canon.why: How every element heavier than helium got made. The paper that ties nuclear physics to the sky.

canon.title: Some Criteria for a Power Producing Thermonuclear Reactor

canon.title: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid

canon.title: A quantitative description of membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in nerve
canon.why: The equations for how a neuron fires. Still the basis of every realistic neuron model.

canon.title: Über den Nachweis und das Verhalten der bei der Bestrahlung des Urans mittels Neutronen entstehenden Erdalkalimetalle
canon.why: The chemistry showing uranium had split into barium. They could not explain it, and published anyway.

canon.title: Disintegration of Uranium by Neutrons: a New Type of Nuclear Reaction
canon.why: The explanation Hahn could not give, worked out over a winter walk. Meitner was left off the Nobel.

canon.title: The Nature of the Chemical Bond

items.title: Detecting Tidal Resonances in Binary Neutron Stars
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: As a binary neutron star inspirals due to the emission of gravitational waves, the rising tidal frequency resonantly excites vibrational modes. These oscillations are seismological probes of the rich stellar interior, yet it remains to be established whether gravitational-wave interferometers can measure them. Here, we present the first fully Bayesian study of the capability of the Einstein Telescope to detect tidal resonances. We simulate one year of observations and analyze the 200 loudest signals. We find that the Einstein Telescope can identify resonant modes and is sensitive to gravitational-wave phase shifts as small as Δ Φ ≈ 0.03 for favorable events. We further show that neglecting resonances can bias the inferred tidal deformabilities. These results establish tidal resonances as a measurable route for asteroseismology with future detectors.

items.title: The Hot Neptune Initiative (HONEI): IV. TOI-4129 b, an Adolescent Neptune in the Ridge
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Recent exoplanet demographics studies have uncovered the Neptune ridge: an overdensity of intermediate-size planets at orbital periods between 3--6~d. The origin of this pile-up remains unclear, but it could be a consequence of high-eccentricity migration (HEM). Here, we confirm TOI-4129\,b, a planet that may help to reveal the origin of the Neptune ridge. Using radial velocities from HARPS-N and transit photometry from TESS and four ground-based telescopes, we found that TOI-4129\,b has a relatively low density ($R_p = 5.7 \pm 0.2\, R_\oplus$, $M_p = 26\pm 6 \,M_\oplus$, $ρ_p = 0.8 \pm 0.2 ~\textrm{g}~\textrm{cm}^{-3}$) and orbits a $V = 12.9$ K dwarf star every 3.27~d, placing it at the inner edge of the Neptune ridge. We detect the stellar rotation period at 12.7~d in the photometry, implying a fairly young gyrochronal age of $1.20^{+0.16}_{-0.30}~$Gyr for the system. With a Transmission Spectroscopy Metric of $112\pm 30$, this adolescent Neptune is a good target for atmospheric observations with \textit{JWST} and \textit{Ariel}, and we also find that it is amenable to future constraints on the (three-dimensional) stellar obliquity. TOI-4129\,b will therefore be an important testing ground for the idea that planets in the Neptune ridge underwent HEM to arrive at their current locations.

items.title: First-principles calculations of far-wing absorption in He-broadened CO2 infrared spectra
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We report theoretical predictions and modeling of the far-wing absorption of CO2 broadened by He over a wide temperature range (200-1000 K), which are relevant for exoplanet atmosphere studies. Accurate modeling of He-broadened CO2 absorption is essential for opacity calculations used to characterize the composition, structure, and climate of exoplanet atmospheres. In particular, the strong CO2 band at 4.3 mum has been clearly identified in the spectra of several exoplanets observed with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). Requantized classical molecular dynamics simulations were first performed to predict absorption in the far wings of the 4.3 mum band of CO2. The resulting predictions show excellent agreement with available experimental data at room temperature. The theoretical predictions and measured data were then used to parameterize an impact energy-corrected sudden model, which allowed us to accurately reproduce the far-wing absorption of He-broadened CO2 in several infrared spectral regions over the (200-1000) K temperature range. Finally, for applications to exoplanet atmosphere opacity calculations, we derived temperature-dependent chi-factor corrections that account for the sub-Lorentzian behavior of the far wing of the major infrared bands of CO2.

items.title: The Korean Space Telescope (KST): A Dedicated Space Observatory for the Dark Universe
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: The Korean Space Telescope (KST) is a next-generation 1.4-meter wide-field space observatory, a dedicated probe of the dark sector. Its single instrument provides diffraction-limited visible imaging (~0.15 arcsec in the optical) together with simultaneous near-infrared (R ~ 100) slitless spectrophotometry, so that every detected source is observed in the NIR by the survey itself, with spectral information delivered at a resolution set by its brightness (full R ~ 100 typing at the bright end, synthetic medium-band or broadband photometry below it) and with no separate follow-up, a capability decisive for time-domain science. With it, KST addresses the three outstanding questions of dark physics in concert: the dynamics of dark energy, the nature of dark matter, and gravitational-wave dark sirens as independent cosmological rulers. KST combines measurements of expansion and structure growth to test dark-energy models. A two-tiered "Wedding Cake" strategy (2,000 deg^2 Wide plus 10 deg^2 cluster-targeted Deep Survey) combines weak lensing, baryon acoustic oscillations, and a near-infrared-standardized Type Ia supernova Hubble diagram to constrain dark energy at its pivot redshift (sigma(w_p) ~ 0.03); maps dark matter from cluster cores to galactic substructure to test cold dark matter against warm and self-interacting alternatives; and builds a deep near-infrared host catalog for a distance-ladder-independent H_0 from dark sirens. The same data yield a Legacy Science portfolio (galaxy evolution, active galactic nuclei, exoplanets, and the Milky Way) at no additional observing cost. As Korea's first dedicated astrophysics space mission, KST occupies a niche complementary to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, Euclid, and Roman.

items.title: Precision Requirements for Robust Small Planet Classification
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Classifying small exoplanets as rocky, volatile-rich, or iron-enriched is a prerequisite for efficient allocation of atmospheric characterization resources. The Nominally Rocky Planet Zone (NRPZ) provides a framework for this classification by comparing observed bulk densities against the expected density range for volatile-free rocky planets, calibrated from stellar abundance distributions. However, the efficacy of classifying a planet using the NRPZ is critically dependent on the precision of the underlying mass and radius measurements. Here, we perform an analytical propagation of observational uncertainties through the NRPZ classification framework for 37 candidate rocky exoplanets with radii below 2 Earth radii orbiting stars with visual magnitudes <11. Among the 37 planets, we find 12 already possess sufficiently precise mass and radius measurements to be confidently classified as Mini-Neptunes or Super-Mercuries. The remaining planets require approximately a ~60% reduction in the combined mass and radius uncertainties before they can be reliably classified. We find that 1-1,000 new observations are necessary to achieve these lower uncertainties, and these are likely lower limits. We argue that, while possible, this level of intense observation is likely not feasible for many of these planets and that mass-radius models alone are not likely to allow us to classify all but those planets with outlier densities. We therefore recommend a staged strategy in which improved mass and radius measurements are used to identify and prioritize ambiguous systems, followed (where feasible) by atmospheric observations with JWST or future facilities as a complementary test of whether selected planets retain substantial atmospheres.

items.title: Nonlinear Phononic Slidetronics
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Layered van der Waals ferroelectrics are conventionally switched by sliding the different layers between stacking orders with opposing electric polarizations. Ultrashort laser pulses have been proposed to launch shear modes and induce switching, with often unfeasible large pulse energies, however. Here, we demonstrate switching of ferroelectricity in bilayer hexagonal boron nitride through nonlinearly excited phonons. We show that the efficiencies of conventional coherent phonon excitation mechanisms, including infrared absorption and Raman scattering techniques, are too low to overcome the energy barrier separating the two ferroelectric states. We demonstrate instead that excitation of high-frequency intralayer modes leads to a tilting of the interlayer potential-energy landscape that enables changing the stacking order. Our results provide an avenue toward efficient phononic slidetronics, enabling ultrafast control of the stacking order in van der Waals materials.

items.abstract: The first evidence of electroweak (EW) production of pairs of Z bosons in association with two jets (jj) in the final state Z Z jj → ℓ ℓ ν ν jj , where ℓ = e , μ , is reported by the CMS experiment. The analysis is based on a data sample of proton-proton ( p p ) collisions at s = 13 TeV , corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb − 1 . Events are selected by requiring exactly two leptons of same flavor and opposite charge, large missing transverse momentum, and two jets with a large rapidity separation and large invariant mass. The EW production cross section in a fiducial volume is σ EW ( p p → Z Z jj → ℓ ℓ ν ν jj ) = 0.3 7 − 0.12 + 0.14 ( stat ) − 0.06 + 0.06 ( syst ) fb , in agreement with the standard model prediction of 0.39 ± 0.06 fb . The observed (expected) significance of the signal is 3.1 (2.8) standard deviations. Limits on anomalous quartic gauge couplings are derived in terms of dimension-8 effective field theory operators. A combination with the previously reported result from the Z Z decay channel with four charged leptons yields an observed (expected) significance of 5.0 (4.5) standard deviations for the EW production of Z boson pairs.

items.abstract: Project 8, a neutrino mass experiment, employs the novel frequency technique of cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy (CRES) to perform a model independent measurement of neutrino mass via tritium beta decay. items.abstract: Martian meteorites provide a record of the planet’s geological history. However, most are geologically young samples that are not representative of Mars’ surface, which is dominated by ancient rocks. We describe the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 (Teg 001), a slowly cooled igneous rock that formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. Its composition, mineralogy, and texture are distinct from other Martian meteorites. We determine that Teg 001 is a sample of ancient crust, which formed from a geochemically distinct mantle source with primordial composition. The presence of aqueously altered minerals, combined with bulk and mineral-specific oxygen isotope measurements, indicate that Teg 001 experienced reactions with fluids enriched in 18 O, before ejection into space by an impact.

items.title: Papaver self-incompatibility is controlled by two multiallelic idiomorphs
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Self-incompatibility (SI) prevents self-fertilization through highly polymorphic genetic recognition at the S locus with multiple alleles. In Papaver rhoeas , the S determinants were previously identified as PrpS and PrsS . However, we found that PrpS-PrsS was absent in many S haplotypes. In this work, we report the identification of an alternative pair of polymorphic S genes, S locus oligopeptide transporter ( SOPT ) and S locus glycine-rich protein ( SGRP ), segregating at the S locus when PrpS-PrsS is absent. SOPT and SGRP display hallmark S determinant features and confer SI when heterologously expressed in Arabidopsis thaliana . Therefore, instead of having allelomorphs with homologous variants, the Papaver SI system is determined by two multiallelic idiomorphs sharing no obvious common ancestry. This discovery of a dual-idiomorph system reveals a distinct genetic basis for polymorphism, with implications for the evolution of allorecognition mechanisms.

items.title: Accurate Charge Radius Measurement of C 14 Confronts Ab Initio Theory
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Located at the neutron shell closure N = 8 , the long-lived radioactive isotope C 14 plays a critical role in geochronology and nuclear structure studies. Despite its widespread use, the nuclear charge radius of C 14 has remained less precisely known than that of its stable counterpart C 12 . Here, we report a high-precision determination of the C 14 charge radius using collinear laser spectroscopy at the COALA setup at TU Darmstadt, improving upon the precision of previous muonic measurements by a factor of 5 and revealing a 1.9 σ discrepancy of combined uncertainty, indicating a likely underestimated uncertainty in the muonic determination. This measurement challenges state-of-the-art nuclear theory calculations, including auxiliary field diffusion Monte Carlo, the valence-space in-medium similarity renormalization group, and the no-core shell model, augmented by neural-network techniques. With C 12 and C 14 now forming one of the most precisely characterized even-even isotope pairs, these results also enable improved QED tests.

items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: We report precise results for the $e^+e^-\to π^+π^-(γ)$ cross section in the energy range between threshold and 1.4 GeV, relevant for the hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon $g-2$ prediction. Using the full 460 fb$^{-1}$ of on- and off-$Υ(4S)$ data, the cross section is derived from the ratio of $π^+π^-$ to $μ^+μ^-$ initial-state radiation (ISR) events, in which many systematic uncertainties cancel. The pion/muon separation does not rely on particle identification as in the 2009 BaBar analysis, but rather makes use of the well-known, different angular distributions in the two-particle center-of-mass system. The compatibility and correlation between the 2026 and 2009 measurements are discussed. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results. The leading-order hadronic contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly calculated using the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements in the energy range of 0.3$-$1.4 GeV are $525.9\pm 3.5_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.8_\mathrm{syst}$ and $517.8\pm 2.4_\mathrm{stat}\pm3.3_\mathrm{syst}$ in units of $10^{-10}$, respectively.

items.title: Toponium hadroproduction at next-to-next-to-leading order in NRQCD

items.abstract: We present the first next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) predictions for inclusive color-singlet toponium hadroproduction within NRQCD in the zero-width limit for the top quark. The central new result is the NNLO QCD correction to the short-distance coefficient for pseudoscalar toponium production. The predictions include electroweak and relativistic corrections, additional production channels, and perturbatively evaluated bound-state matrix elements. At the Large Hadron Collider proton-proton center-of-mass energy of $13\,\mathrm{TeV}$, we obtain a cross section of $4.87^{+0.63}_{-0.65}\,\mathrm{pb}$, with scale and parametric uncertainties combined. The NNLO corrections reduce the renormalization- and factorization-scale uncertainties by approximately a factor of four relative to NLO, to the few-percent level. The dominant remaining uncertainty arises from the Coulomb-scale dependence of the bound-state matrix elements.

items.title: $Φ$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Quantifying selection effects in gravitational-wave population studies requires millions of costly signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) calculations. We present $Φ$asmaNet, a compact neural architecture for structured tabular regression, with staged spectral refinement as an explicit architectural prior. Learned input tokens are refined through ordered attention-based $Φ$-Stages, each augmented by a $Φ$-Refractor subspace-mixing module, then revisited through gated top-down $Φ$-Feedback. Applied to the 11-dimensional parameters of precessing, higher-mode binary black hole signals (IMRPhenomXPHM), it predicts phase-averaged optimal SNR for a single detector at fixed Advanced LIGO design sensitivity. With approximately 732k parameters, it outperforms MLP, 1D-ResNet and Transformer-encoder baselines under matched training across $10^5$--$10^6$ samples. At $10^6$ samples, it achieves $100-\mathrm{MAPE}=98.73\%$ on the held-out test set, $99.29\%$ after rank-preserving monotonic (PCHIP) calibration, and $99.39\%$ ($R^2=0.9998$) in the detection-relevant regime $ρ>8$, with stable accuracy across independent dataset realizations. On a single GPU, it sustains approximately $1.2\times10^5$ SNR evaluations per second and processes a $10^6$-injection catalogue end-to-end in approximately 8.3 s, about two orders of magnitude faster than conventional waveform-and-inner-product calculations on a 16-core CPU. Exact distance rescaling through $ρ\propto1/d_L$ supports repeated catalogue-wide detectability evaluations. The fully documented pipeline is intended as a reproducible benchmark, while results on public tabular datasets indicate competitiveness beyond gravitational-wave applications. Although demonstrated for a fixed single-detector configuration, the construction supports extensions to detector networks and epoch-specific sensitivities. (Abridged)

items.title: Magnetic shocks generated by two counterstreaming plasma jets induced by an intense femtosecond laser pulse
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: This work extends the investigation of magnetic control of counterstreaming laser-produced plasma jets reported in Zemskov et al. (2026), focusing on the experiments performed in the presence of a uniform 14 T magnetic field oriented transverse to the jet propagation. When generating plasma flows using 60-80 fs, 10-15 J pulses at the PEARL facility, we observe the formation of narrow, stationary layers with strong magnetic-field amplification and sharp plasma-density gradients in the interaction region. We interpret these features as the result of compressing the externally applied transverse field by the converging plasma ram pressure. The external magnetic field is advected and compressed until its magnetic pressure balances the decreasing ram pressure of the jets. Time-resolved interferometry, shadowgraphy, and Faraday polarimetry, combined with hybrid PIC--fluid simulations, reproduce the formation of a high-field barrier that decelerates and laterally redirects plasma flows while producing multiple density jumps. We discuss the astrophysical implications: the compression of an initially weak ambient field by converging flows provides an efficient, non-turbulent channel for magnetic-field amplification that can render interstellar magnetic fields dynamically important - a condition essential for diffusive shock acceleration in supernova remnants. Our experiments therefore establish a laboratory platform bridging externally magnetized and self-magnetized regimes and offer a complementary route to magnetic-field amplification in high-energy astrophysical shocks.

items.title: Options for heating, fueling, and current drive in MANTA, a high-field negative triangularity fusion pilot plant
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: In this work, we assess how the performance of MANTA, a high-field, highly radiative, negative triangularity tokamak concept, depends on pellet fueling, ion cyclotron resonant frequency (ICRF) heating, and lower hybrid current drive (LHCD) schemes. Negative triangularity (NT) has been gaining momentum in the fusion community as a naturally, robustly ELM-free regime that is capable of power plant level performance. The MANTA device has been the subject of previous works regarding the whole-device design, power handling and divertor assessments, and core transport optimizations. Informed by these previous studies, we assess whether changes to the original MANTA heating and current drive scheme can positively affect performance, both in terms of lowering scrape-off layer power (improving power-handling, a primary benefit of NT) and maximizing plasma gain to levels necessary for an attractive fusion pilot plant. In this work, we find that the MANTA concept can yield improved performance in terms of plasma gain and scrape-off layer power by simultaneously going to lower input power and higher seeded impurity fraction. Also, we find that increasing the fueling magnitude can increase fusion power while minimally impacting scrape-off layer power. Performance can also be improved by optimizing the ICRF design; decreasing the minority ion fraction, decreasing the toroidal mode number of the injected wave, and switching from a helium-3 minority ion to a hydrogen-1 minority ion all result in increases to fusion power. The additional inboard space afforded by the NT geometry provides an opportunity for wave launch to be moved to the inboard side. This is beneficial for LHCD access and results in a wide range of potential current profiles in the edge, with the total driven current due to 25 MW of LHCD reaching up to 1.2 MA, or about 12% of the total current.

items.title: El Agente Fármaco: A Scalable AI Scientist for Drug Discovery
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Computational drug discovery offers a growing range of tools for proposing and evaluating molecules, but combining them and deciding what to do next still requires substantial expert effort. Here, we introduce El Agente Fármaco, an AI scientist that uses modern large language model (LLM) technology to turn discovery goals expressed in everyday language into complex, scalable computational screening workflows. The agentic harness selects scientific tools, reviews their results, and adjusts subsequent steps to the target and the user's objectives. Our approach centers on a shared scientific memory: Fármaco Atlas, which stores molecules, structures, and results together with their provenance -- a record of how they were obtained. The agent uses targeted database queries to retrieve the evidence needed for each decision. A single request can launch calculations for an entire collection of molecules, without requiring a separate LLM decision for every compound. This design limits the information the model must process as screening collections grow, while keeping the underlying results available for inspection and further analysis. The integrated tools support molecule generation, prediction of binding and molecular properties, and searches for compounds available for purchase. In a retrospective comparison with an expert-led campaign, the agent proposed chemically distinct candidates with competitive docking scores and higher calculated drug-likeness under explicitly imposed selection criteria. In a 22-task benchmark against plain tool calls and Codex, the agent achieved the highest observed mean model-judged score, with lower median cumulative token use and peak context. Fármaco provides a foundation for flexible, scalable drug discovery workflows that connect scientific reasoning with an enduring, traceable record of computational work.

items.title: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every step is a Born measurement - attention $|\langle q|k\rangle|^4$ normalised over each row, a measured product in place of the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout. With its denominators held at their values for the input, each class probability is a polynomial in the word amplitudes, so its integrated-gradient evidence is computed by a finite quadrature with no quadrature error: the words' contributions sum to the class probability above its no-information share, to $10^{-11}$ or better. On e-SNLI natural language inference, with about 98k parameters outside the embedding, the model reaches $76.98 \pm 0.17$% test accuracy, level with a softmax transformer of the same size ($76.62 \pm 0.36$%). Deleting the word its evidence ranks first changes the answer in 45% of test pairs, out of the 53% any single deletion can change, against 32% for the softmax model explained the same way and 40% by its attention x gradient. Attention can look more like the words annotators highlighted, yet accounts for the answer less well: deleting the word it ranks first changes the Born Transformer's answer in 32% of pairs. The same weights compile exactly to optoelectronic optics and to qubits, and a coherent attention layer becomes one circuit equal to the model (852 CNOTs on 23 qubits). On IBM's ibm_kingston, reading only the attention overlaps by Hadamard tests, the device gave the model's answers on two short test pairs and kept or changed them under deletion as the model does; the evidence itself did not yet survive the device, and we work out the shots and calibration that measuring it on hardware would need.

items.title: Weight-space programming for auditing clinical decision networks
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Machine learning models in radiotherapy are commissioned by testing them on cases with known answers, which may not reveal a shortcut that the test cases share with the training data. Frontier language models have recently been reported to read and write the raw weights of small neural networks, an ability called weight-space programming. The purpose of this study was to determine whether such a model, given only a clinical protocol and a network's weights, can audit and repair the network. Networks with 433 to 4,801 parameters were trained to screen head-and-neck planning requests against four rules. Flaws were planted through the training data: confounds that hid each rule, a 3 Gy shift in the cord threshold, and a hidden trigger. Claude Opus 5.5 audited each network blind, without tools, data or code execution, and every claim and repair was tested on about 420,000 requests. The language model named the broken rule in 16 of 18 flawed networks (95% CI 67% to 97%), including all 15 with a confound or a threshold shift. It repaired each of the 16 by changing a median of 3 parameters. Fine-tuning on protocol-labeled requests also repaired every network, but changed nearly every parameter. Each confound and shift it found was visible in single units, and a simple statistic chosen for each flaw type found the same flaws. It cleared 2 of 5 healthy networks without being forced and found 1 of 3 triggers. Testing against the protocol detected every flaw, and black-box testing found the confounds and the shift faster. The results indicate that, in small networks, weight-space programming can locate and repair flaws that silence an input or shift a threshold, but cannot yet certify that a network is correct.

items.title: Global sensitivity analysis for stochastic models of infectious diseases: Re-emergence of yellow fever virus in the Americas as a case study
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Nate Kornetzke, Helen J. Wearing Emerging infectious diseases are a persistent public health threat that challenge deterministic, mechanistic modeling approaches. Because outbreaks initially start with a low number of infected hosts, their dynamics are highly stochastic, making traditional deterministic methods, e.g., ordinary differential equations, unable to qualitatively or quantitatively capture the transmission dynamics. In place, stochastic models are used, such as Markov chain models, but these models present their own challenges. Often, to infer a quantity of interest with stochastic models, we need to sample the model’s distribution many times over, introducing an additional source of noise to our analysis. This additional noise makes the inference of our quantity of interest more difficult and computationally expensive. Here, we show how novel tools from the field of uncertainty quantification can be used to efficiently separate these two channels of noise, allowing us to make rigorous statistical inferences about processes important for disease emergence. We illustrate these techniques with a model of yellow fever virus spillover in the Americas, a virus that has seen rapid re-emergence amongst multiple hosts and vectors in South America over the last decade. items.title: Modeling runaway electron mitigation via passively driven plasma instabilities in a high-current tokamak
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: A critical challenge for tokamak-based fusion power plants is the formation of high-current, relativistic runaway electron (RE) beams during abrupt confinement loss events called disruptions. RE beams may significantly damage machine components if left unmitigated, jeopardizing the operational and economic viability of fusion power plants. We present the first self-consistent extended magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) computational study of RE mitigation with a passively driven RE mitigation coil (REMC) in a high-current tokamak. RE generation and transport are coupled with REMC-driven MHD activity in a 3D simulation that models the thermal and current quench phases of a mid-plane disruption, together with the vertical displacement and final termination of the plasma and RE beam on SPARC -- a high-field, high-current tokamak designed to achieve a fusion gain Q > 1. We demonstrate that REMC-driven magnetic stochasticity can reduce the RE current by over an order-of-magnitude when compared to unmitigated disruptions. The final termination is mediated via a post-thermal-quench "cold" vertical displacement of the plasma, which, together with magnetic stochasticity, increases RE losses via scrape-off once the plasma contacts the first wall. These results demonstrate a viable mechanism for RE mitigation using passively driven plasma instabilities on high-current tokamaks.

items.title: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning–assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth–based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.

items.title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development—its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

items.title: A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: At the skin’s surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E 2 , which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

items.title: One-minute frequency disturbances from unintended synchronization in cyber–physical power systems
items.license: Crossref metadata CC0; abstract as deposited by publisher
items.abstract: Electric power systems are evolving into cyber–physical infrastructures shaped by power electronics and digital control. As inverter-based generation alters system dynamics and digitalization heightens vulnerability to errors and attacks, cyber–physical coupling can also introduce subtle system-level effects. Here we show that grid-frequency time series worldwide exhibit a persistent 1-min oscillatory pattern whose origin has remained unexplained. We show that clock-synchronized control software in digitally controlled energy devices, particularly uninterruptible power supplies and battery energy storage systems, generates periodic power-demand peaks that propagate across voltage levels and can give rise to the observed pattern. The pattern amplitude has increased substantially in several grids over recent years, contributing to wear and tear in hydropower systems and motivating stricter frequency-control requirements. The rapid expansion of battery storage, data centres and the Internet-of-Things may further amplify such cyber–physical power oscillations, highlighting the need for improved control design.

items.title: Glutamate receptor composition at Drosophila neuromuscular junctions depends on developmental stage and muscle identity
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: The neuromuscular junction (NMJ) of larval Drosophila is widely used for studying synaptic transmission. Larval body wall muscles express five ionotropic glutamate receptor (iGluR) subunits that assemble into two tetrameric complexes, with subunit composition determining the strength and plasticity of synaptic transmission. Because NMJ function has been extensively characterized in larvae, it has commonly been assumed that adult fly NMJs share this molecular composition, despite substantial differences between life stages. Here, we systematically compare glutamate receptor expression across larval and adult Drosophila muscles. We find that adult leg and flight muscles exhibit different iGluR expression than larvae, lacking expression of several receptors previously considered essential. Adjacent muscles within the adult femur express distinct iGluRs, suggesting specialization of flexor and extensor muscles. Finally, the glutamate-gated chloride channel (GluClα) is expressed extrasynaptically in adult but not larval muscle fibers. Our results reveal unexpected heterogeneity in glutamate receptor expression across muscles and developmental stages, demonstrating the need for muscle-specific analyses in flies and other animals.

items.title: Transient feedforward communication between somatosensory and premotor cortex supports goal-directed behavior
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Yadollah Ranjbar-Slamloo, Tsukasa Kamigaki Goal-directed behavior requires sensory information to be transformed into motor commands, yet the precise temporal structure of communication between sensory and motor cortices during this process remains poorly understood. By simultaneously recording spiking activity from primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and secondary motor cortex (M2) in mice performing a tactile delayed go/no-go task, we identified a brief, stimulus-triggered communication window that predicted behavioral success. This transient interaction conveyed stimulus-selective information such that the S1 → M2 communication subspace aligned with stimulus-coding axes in both regions. In contrast, M2 → S1 feedback interactions were weaker and delayed. Brief optogenetic suppression of S1 reduced both M2 stimulus selectivity and behavioral discriminability, consistent with a functional role of the transient S1 → M2 coupling. items.title: Automatic Generation of Novel Highly-Functional Molecular Sequences
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: While multiple methods now exist to generate functional sequence variants from existing annotated examples, it is unclear how well such methods can be used to generate sequences that exceed the functionality of those contained in the example set. Using two complete fitness landscapes, we quantify how effectively generative tools can search sequence space and find rare, novel, highly functional sequences, focusing on variational auto-encoders and information-theoretic methods. We find that an information-theoretic method that does not require training and runs significantly faster than standard Machine-Learning/Artificial Intelligence (ML/AI) methods also is significantly more effective in finding rare highly-functional sequences. We discuss the application of this novel method to discover rare polypeptides with anti-bacterial properties that are specific to bacterial, but not eukaryotic, cell membranes.

items.title: Emotion knowledge is structured in a grid-like coordinate system in the human ventromedial prefrontal cortex
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Yumeng Ma, Philip A. Kragel Human emotional experiences vary widely in everyday life, yet they are systematically organized within a continuous affective space defined by valence and arousal. Although this circumplex organization has shaped decades of research, its neural implementation remains unclear. Here, we asked whether abstract emotion concepts are encoded using grid-like coordinate principles in the human brain. During fMRI, participants tracked trajectories through affective space conveyed through morphs of facial expressions and sequences of phrases. We found that ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) encoded affective space with robust hexadirectional modulation characteristic of grid-like coding. This coordinate representation generalized across stimulus modalities, indicating abstraction beyond perceptual features. The grid-like signal reflected a metric organization of emotion concepts independent of overt behavior, whereas distance-related signals in vmPFC predicted trial-by-trial affective judgements. Together, these findings suggest that emotion knowledge is structured by a grid-like coordinate system in the human brain that can support predictive inference and flexible decision-making.

items.title: Estimating bone marrow adiposity from head MRI and identifying its genetic architecture
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Bone marrow (BM) adiposity changes radically through the lifespan, but this phenomenon is poorly characterized and understood in humans. Large datasets of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans of the head have been collected to study the human brain, but also contain unexploited information about other organs. We developed an artificial neural network that localizes calvarial BM in T1-weighted MRI head scans, enabling us to study its composition in several large MRI datasets, and to model sex-dimorphic age trajectories, including the effect of menopause. We revealed high heritability in single-nucleotide polymorphism and twin data, and identified 41 genetic loci significantly associated with the trait, including six sex-specific loci. Integrating mapped genes with existing BM single-cell RNA-sequencing data revealed patterns of adipogenic lineage differentiation and lipid loading. Finally, we identified significant genetic correlations with several human traits, including cognitive ability and Parkinson’s disease, which is intriguing in light of the recently discovered channels that link calvarial BM to the meninges.

items.title: Targeting tankyrase scaffolding in the β-catenin destruction complex by PROTAC overcomes the limitation of catalytic inhibitors in colorectal cancer
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Aberrant WNT/β-catenin signaling drives tumorigenesis and metastasis in cancer. Although enzymatic inhibitors of tankyrase (TNKS) effectively block AXIN degradation and stabilize the β-catenin destruction complex (DC), they have demonstrated limited efficacy in various colorectal cancer (CRC) models. Here, we demonstrate that, unexpectedly, the induction of AXIN puncta represents a major barrier to achieving therapeutic efficacy. Mechanistically, catalytic inhibition of TNKS prevents TNKS turnover and drives its accumulation in the DC, wherein the scaffolding function of TNKS induces AXIN puncta formation, rigidifies the DC, and impedes β-catenin turnover. Chemically induced degradation of TNKS overcomes this limitation by stabilizing AXIN without puncta formation, providing a deeper suppression of the WNT/β-catenin pathway activity and the proliferation of CRC cells harboring dysfunctional APC mutations. Collectively, these findings provide an explanation for the unsatisfactory outcomes of drugging the WNT/β-catenin signaling pathway by TNKS inhibitors and highlight TNKS degradation as a promising approach to treat WNT/β-catenin-driven CRC.

items.title: Knockdown of a regulatory barcode shifts macrophage polarization destination from M1 to M2 and increases pathogen burden upon S. aureus infection
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Macrophages are driven to form distinct functional phenotypes in response to different immunological stimuli, in a process widely referred to as macrophage polarization. Transcriptional regulators that guide macrophage polarization in response to a given trigger remain largely unknown. items.license: CC BY 4.0 (stated on each paper page)
items.abstract: Quantum 10, 2258 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-11-03-2258 QwaveMPS is an open-source Python library for simulating one-dimensional quantum many-body waveguide systems using matrix product states (MPS). It provides a user-friendly interface for constructing, evolving, and analyzing quantum states and operators, facilitating studies in quantum physics and quantum information with waveguide-QED systems. This approach enables efficient, scalable simulations by focusing computational resources on the most relevant parts of the quantum system. Thus, one can study a wide range of complex dynamical interactions, including time-delayed feedback effects in the non-Markovian regime and deeply nonlinear systems, at a highly reduced computational cost compared to full Hilbert space approaches, making it both practical and convenient to model a variety of open waveguide-QED systems (in Markovian and non-Markovian regimes), treating quantized atoms and quantized photons on an equal footing. items.title: Distinct gradients of cortical architecture capture visual representations and behavior across the lifespan
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: The microstructure of cells within the human cerebral cortex varies across the cortical ribbon, where changes in cytoarchitecture and myeloarchitecture are thought to endow each region of the cortex with its unique function. While fine-scale relative to a cell, these changes at the population level impact architectural properties of the cortex measurable in vivo by noninvasive MRI, such as the thickness and myelin content of the cortex. This raises the question of whether or not we can use these in vivo architectural measures to understand cortical organization, function, and development more broadly. Using the human visual cortex as a test bed, we demonstrated two architectural gradients, one in which cytoarchitecture and myeloarchitecture converge and another in which they diverge. These two gradients underlie the structural and functional topography of the visual cortex, even predicting the presence of new visual representations. Moreover, the two gradients show distinct visual behavior relevance and lifespan trajectory. These findings provide a more general framework for understanding the human cortex, showing that architectural gradients are a measurable fingerprint of functional organization and ontogenetic routines in the human brain.

items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Michal Pecho, Josef Tkadlec, Martin A. Nowak Evolution occurs in populations of reproducing individuals. In stochastic descriptions of evolutionary dynamics, such as the Moran process, individuals are chosen randomly for birth and for death. If the same type is chosen for both steps, then the reproductive event is wasted, because the composition of the population remains unchanged. Here we introduce a new phenotype, which we call a replacer . Replacers are efficient competitors. When a replacer is chosen for reproduction, the offspring will always replace an individual of another type (if available). We determine the selective advantage of replacers in well-mixed populations and on one-dimensional lattices. We find that being a replacer substantially boosts the fixation probability of neutral and deleterious mutants. In particular, fixation probability of a single neutral replacer who invades a well-mixed population of size N is of the order of 1/N rather than the standard 1/ N . Even more importantly, replacers are much better protected against invasions once they have reached fixation. Therefore, replacers dominate the mutation selection equilibrium even if the phenotype of being a replacer comes at a substantial cost: curiously, for large population sizes and small mutation rates, the relative reproductive rate of a successful replacer can be as low as 1/ e .

items.title: Macroscopic quantum coherence and entanglement in mechanical systems
items.license: CC BY 4.0 (stated on each paper page)
items.abstract: Quantum 10, 2257 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-10-30-2257 The notion of a macroscopic quantum state must be pinned down in order to assess how well experiments probe the large-scale limits of quantum mechanics. However, the issue of quantifying so-called quantum macroscopicity is fraught with multiple approaches having varying interpretations and levels of computability and measurability. Here, we introduce two measures that capture independent macroscopic properties: i) extensive size, measuring the degree of coherence in position or momentum observables relative to atomic-scale units, and ii) entangled size, quantifying the number of entangled subsystems. These measures unify many desirable features of past proposals while having rigorously justified interpretations from quantum information theory in terms of coherence and multipartite entanglement. We demonstrate how to estimate them and obtain lower-bounds using experimental data from micro-mechanical oscillators and diffracting molecules. Notably, we find evidence for genuine multipartite entanglement of $10^5$ to $10^7$ atoms in recent mechanical superposition states.

items.title: Re-uploading quantum data: a universal function approximator for quantum inputs
items.license: CC BY 4.0 (stated on each paper page)
items.abstract: Quantum 10, 2256 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-10-29-2256 Quantum data re-uploading has proved powerful for classical inputs, where repeatedly encoding features into a small circuit yields universal function approximation. Extending this idea to quantum inputs remains underexplored, as the information contained in a quantum state is not directly accessible in classical form. We propose and analyze a quantum data re-uploading architecture in which a qubit interacts sequentially with fresh copies of an arbitrary input state. The circuit can approximate any bounded continuous function using only one ancilla qubit and single-qubit measurements, provided that sufficiently many copies of the input state and, in general, sufficiently many layers are available. By alternating entangling unitaries with mid-circuit resets of the input register, the architecture realizes a discrete cascade of completely positive and trace-preserving maps, analogous to collision models in open quantum system dynamics. Our framework provides a space-efficient and expressive approach to designing quantum machine learning models that operate directly on quantum data.

items.abstract: Quantum 10, 2252 (2026). https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2026-10-28-2252 We show that recent experiments in hybrid qubit-oscillator devices that measure the phase-space characteristic function of the oscillator via the qubit can be seen through the lens of functional calculus and path integrals, drawing a clear analogy with the generating functional of a quantum field theory. This connection suggests an expansion of the characteristic function in terms of Feynman diagrams, exposing the role of the real-time bosonic propagator, and identifying the external source functions with certain time-dependent couplings that can be controlled experimentally. By applying maximum-likelihood techniques, we show that the “measurement'' of these Feynman diagrams can be reformulated as a problem of multi-parameter point estimation that takes as input a set of Ramsey-type measurements of the qubit. By numerical simulations that consider leading imperfections in trapped-ion devices, we identify the optimal regimes in which Feynman diagrams could be reconstructed from measured data with low systematic and stochastic errors. We discuss how these ideas can be generalized to finite temperatures via the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, contributing to a bottom-up approach to probe quantum simulators of lattice field theories by systematically increasing the qubit-oscillator number.

items.title: Class-wide sequence, structural, and docking-profile diversity of insect odorant receptors and structural specialization of Orco

items.abstract: Insect olfaction is facilitated by a heterotetrameric odorant receptor–odorant receptor co-receptor (OR-Orco) complex. However, extensive sequence divergence and lineage-specific expansion have complicated large-scale comparisons of OR repertoires across insects. Here, we integrated sequence similarity, structural similarity, and molecular docking to analyze ORs from 115 insect species. OR repertoire size was associated with adult diet, larval diet, and habitat, but not with circadian rhythm. We developed a ‘trunk–branch’ network framework to classify ORs according to sequence and structural similarity and used large-scale molecular docking to derive comparative docking profiles. Despite marked differences in sequence- and structural-community composition, almost all sampled orders contained ORs assigned to all six docking-profile communities. Holometabolous insects showed higher OR sequence-community diversity than non-holometabolous insects, and docking-profile composition differed between extant lineages whose order-level origins predate or postdate the end-Permian mass extinction. Most notably, we identified a highly conserved extracellular β-sheet in Orco that restricts ligand access to the binding pocket and may contribute to its reduced capacity to bind natural odorants. items.title: Spyglass is a framework for reproducible and shareable neuroscience research
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Scientific progress depends on reliable and reproducible results. Progress can be accelerated when data are shared and re-analyzed to address new questions. Current approaches to storing and analyzing neural data involve bespoke formats and software that make replication and reuse of data difficult. To address these challenges, we created Spyglass, an open-source data management and analysis framework written in Python. Spyglass provides reproducible pipelines for common neuroscience analyses and sharing of raw data, intermediate analyses, and final results within and across labs. Spyglass uses the Neurodata Without Borders (NWB) standard and includes pipelines for spectral filtering, spike sorting, pose tracking, and neural decoding. Spyglass can be extended to apply existing and newly developed pipelines to datasets from multiple sources. We demonstrate these features in the context of a cross-laboratory replication by applying advanced state space decoding algorithms to publicly available data. New users can try out Spyglass on a Jupyter Hub hosted by HHMI and 2i2c: https://spyglass.hhmi.2i2c.cloud/ .

items.title: Visualization and Characterization of Gene Group Distribution Patterns Across Genomes
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Genes of the same family often lie close together on a chromosome, yet how far apart family members sit, and whether their spacing follows any pattern, has rarely been measured consistently across genomes. We built an interactive web application that places the members of any of the 1,396 FlyBase gene groups on the banded ideogram of the fruit fly (Drosophila melanogaster) and lists each member's neighbours. While browsing it, we found strikingly symmetric gene sets in which consecutive members are almost evenly spaced. In the RAB GTPases, two 5.08 Mb spacings differ by only 634 bp. We also found that distances between neighbouring members fall into two populations: short-range (median 1.8 kb) and long-range (median 2.4 Mb). Although an arm-matched random control suggests that the even spacing (without a minimum-distance filter) as well as the long-range population arise largely by chance, the short-range population turns out to be a genuine clustering signal. We then extended the analysis to human and six other model organisms (mouse, zebrafish, Caenorhabditis elegans, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Arabidopsis thaliana and maize), and every genome showed the same two populations. The mixture curve of the two is nearly constant across chromosomes in some genomes (Type I: fly, maize, Arabidopsis, C. elegans) but varies across chromosomes in others (Type II: human, mouse, zebrafish, yeast). Thus, across eight eukaryotes, family members lie in two distance populations. The scale of the short-range population follows the spacing of genes in each genome, and the long-range population matches random placement in fly and is consistent with it in the other genomes. Our results also show that visual patterns such as even spacing must be tested against chance before they are interpreted. Our tool and approach give a simple way to explore and compare gene clustering across species.

items.title: In-depth data movement characterization of DNA read mapping algorithms
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Read mapping algorithms represent a critical bottleneck in genomic analysis pipelines due to the resources required; a problem that is becoming more pronounced as sequencing technologies advance and datasets expand. We present an extensive workload characterization of leading read mapping algorithms across diverse sequencing technologies to identify hardware acceleration and optimization opportunities. We analyzed the following implementations: MashMap, wfmash, and Minimap2 for whole-genome alignment (WGA); NGMLR, Minimap2, and LRA for long reads; and Bowtie2, BWA-MEM, StrobeAlign, and minibwa for short reads. We used the Intel VTune Profiler for detailed memory analysis to identify memory- bound functions, cache usage patterns, and data transfer bottlenecks. We further analyzed a selected subset of alignment tools using the DAMOV-SIM simulator to obtain a more granular view of data movement characteristics for two different cache structures. Based on our results, Minimap2 emerges as the fastest alignment tool for long read scenarios, but falls behind in whole-genome alignment due to poor multithreading. Across all three categories, some programs (e.g., LRA, BWA-MEM) are highly memory-bound. More in-depth analysis via DAMOV-SIM revealed that some memory-bound tools, in particular, do not fully utilize the multi-level cache hierarchy in modern multi-core CPU architectures. Our results show that while some tools require algorithmic redesign for performance gains, some others can benefit from running on PIM architectures.

items.title: SpatioCAD: Context-aware graph diffusion model for pinpointing spatially variable genes in heterogeneous tissues
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Hao Wen, Qunlun Shen, Shuqin Zhang Spatial transcriptomics enables comprehensive characterization of tissue architecture, and the identification of spatially variable genes (SVGs) is a critical step for defining region-specific molecular markers and uncovering spatially regulated mechanisms across diverse biological contexts. However, most existing methods for SVG detection overlook cell density variations, a major confounding factor in complex tissues such as tumors, where heterogeneous cellularity frequently introduces false-positive calls. Here we present SpatioCAD, a computational framework that explicitly decouples genuine spatial expression patterns from confounding effects driven by cellularity. SpatioCAD introduces a graph diffusion model that inherently incorporates cell-density-aware conditions to simulate expression propagation, supporting the identification of SVGs across a broad range of expression levels. Systematic evaluations on simulated datasets demonstrate its superior statistical power and specificity. Applied to breast cancer, lung cancer, and glioma datasets, SpatioCAD identifies functionally diverse SVGs, including low‑abundance transcripts with established roles in tumor progression, while also recapitulates biologically meaningful tissue architecture features. Importantly, SpatioCAD is fast and scalable to large tissues.

items.title: Pin and Replay, or Refuse: Conditional Exactness and Probabilistic Validation Across Reference Releases
items.license: arXiv API terms; metadata CC0
items.abstract: Biologists annotate genomes by searching proteins against reference databases such as Pfam, which publish new releases every few weeks to months. Each release forces a full re-search, though most of the database is unchanged: 86.6% of Pfam entries matched between releases 38.1 and 38.2 after excluding build metadata and comments. Reusing old results is hard because search programs are fixed binaries whose printed statistics depend on whole-database size. We present TARE (Tool Annotation Replay with Evidence), a wrapper that reruns an unmodified program only on entries that can matter, pinning the program's database-size setting to the new release so it prints the numbers a full run would print. TARE then tests the replay by adding back omitted entries and refuses with a failure status if any line changes, dumping a full stock body when the tool still runs. Two claims stay separate: conditional exactness under a stated contract (tested each update, not proved), and runtime assurance as probabilistic validation at a stated prevalence---not a guarantee against shipping incorrect output. In the all-record timing, TARE audits 299 records from all queries, so a hidden dependency affecting at least 1% of that population ships with probability at most 5% (valid oracle); rarer faults are outside that bound. On Pfam 38.1->38.2, TARE is 3.47x faster than a full rerun under that audit (median over 8 genomes after excluding 1 flagged genome; 95% CI 3.30-3.81). Historical candidate-population timings on the same nine genomes were 4.24x (Bernoulli; 95% CI 4.17-4.68) and 3.49x (bounded s=299; 95% CI 3.32-4.10). Cost of checking versus unchecked replay is 1.58x (C/B). Across 715,704 HMMER and Infernal output lines, none differed from a full run. TARE refused DIAMOND, whose first filter reads neighboring database bytes, and BLAST+, whose unpinned probe rows fit none of TARE's column rules.

items.title: Oxytocin neurons signal state-dependent transitions from rest to thermogenesis and behavioral arousal
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: Core body temperature (Tb) is defended within narrow limits through thermoregulatory behaviors like huddling, nesting, and physical activity, as well as autonomic responses like brown fat thermogenesis. While Tb displays regulated fluctuations across different behavioral states and rest/arousal cycles, the neural control of these transitions remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the relationship between oxytocin neurons of the paraventricular hypothalamus (PVN OT ) and behavioral and autonomic thermoeffector pathways across physiological states in mice. First, we show that PVN OT neurons are activated during social thermoregulation. We then demonstrate that in vivo PVN OT calcium dynamics align with transitions from rest to thermogenesis and behavioral arousal. Counter to our initial hypothesis, these dynamics were observed in both social and non-social contexts. Using a computer vision model to track thermoeffector pathways, we demonstrate that precisely timed stimulation of PVN OT neurons during low-Tb resting states increases thermogenesis followed by behavioral arousal. We therefore suggest a model in which PVN OT neurons facilitate homeostatic state-dependent transitions in thermo-behavioral states.

items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: The molecular mechanisms that drive (lymph-)angiogenesis are crucial to understanding diseases, such as lymphedema, that are caused due to malformations of the lymphatic vasculature. Recently, an interaction between the secreted protein Svep1, a key regulator in lymphangiogenesis, and the transmembrane receptor Tie1 was shown in zebrafish, humans, and mice. Here, guided by in silico AlphaFold-multimer structure predictions of SVEP1 complexes, we assert with protein binding studies that the human CCP20 domain is the primary binding site for TIE1. We further demonstrate that SVEP1 mediates strong binding of ANG2 and TIE1, and that combined stimulation of hdLECs with SVEP1 and ANG2 leads to phosphorylation of TIE1. TIE1 activation by SVEP1 and ANG2 enables downstream signaling and, in turn, potentiates nuclear exclusion of FOXO1 and phosphorylation of AKT compared to SVEP1 or ANG2 alone. We present a model in which ANG1/2 dimers bind to both SVEP1 and TIE1, resulting in the recruitment of multiple TIE1 receptor molecules to a multimeric complex at the cell membrane, potentially amplifying its signaling capacity.

items.abstract: by Kang Wang, Chun-Lai Ren, Yu-Qiang Ma DEAD-box RNA helicases (DDXs) are traditionally known as ATP-dependent motors that unwind double-stranded RNA (dsRNA). Recent experiments, however, show that some DDXs promote dsRNA unwinding even in the absence of ATP, raising a fundamental question about the physical mechanism underlying ATP-independent strand separation. Here, we develop a minimal, physics-based coarse-grained RNA model and incorporate weak, specific interactions between DDX3X and dsRNA, revealing the inherently stochastic nature of unwinding events. The unwinding process must overcome an energy barrier, but thermal fluctuations and entropy gain provide a driving force for RNA remodeling. We identify that dsRNA separation proceeds through rare yet obligatory strand-displacing intermediates facilitated by DDX3X. By combining deep learning-assisted analysis, we further rank the contributions of different entropic components, revealing hydrogen bonding as the dominant factor, followed by base stacking and then the backbone conformation. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized physical mechanism for RNA duplex unwinding and offer an effective framework for studying RNA remodeling kinetics.

items.title: Ten simple rules for teaching practical AI to health data teams
items.license: CC BY 4.0
items.abstract: by Eric Just, Aik Choon Tan Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly entered the healthcare discourse, often framed through the lens of frontier models, generative systems, and transformative potential. Yet for many healthcare data teams, the practical path from curiosity to capability remains unclear. Concerns about data privacy, regulatory compliance, brittle systems, and misaligned expectations frequently stall progress before meaningful experimentation can begin. This paper presents ten simple rules for teaching practical AI to healthcare data teams, grounded in real-world data, privacy-first experimentation, and system-level thinking. Drawing on hands-on training experiences and existing educational and methodological literature, we argue that AI education in healthcare must prioritize workflows over models, systems over components, and institutional capability over isolated technical success. These rules are intended to help educators and organizational leaders move teams beyond the AI hype cycle toward building trustworthy, sustainable, and context-aware AI systems that matter.
